findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The ice scoop in the upstairs bar was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This allows for bare hand contact with a ready to eat food, ice, when the employee grabs the handle of the scoop. The PIC was shown and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that all utensils are stored so that the read to eat foods are protected from bare hand contact moving forward.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical or temperature SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) On arrival the dish machine in the bar area would not register correct chemical sanitizer concentration on either the facility’s or inspector’s tests trips. The machine could not be brought into compliance during the inspection. The PIC contacted their EcoLab rep who stated that they would arrive in approximately one to two days to conducted maintenance. The inspector will follow up in three days to verify the maintinance has been completed. A card was left with the PIC. They should contact the inspector if there is an issue with the repair that needs more time. Until the repair can be completed the dishes produced at this location should be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitized) in another location or method. 
2) (REPEAT) On arrival the dish machine in the kitchen would not register correct sanitizer for either the temperature or chemical variations that the PIC indicated should be in effect. The machine was eventually brought into compliance by changing the CL concentrate jug and manually priming the machine.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a food handler touch arugula with their bare hands on the kitchen prep line. CORRECTED- the item was removed from service to be discarded. Ensure all ready to eat foods and garnishes are handled with washed and gloved hands to prevent contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine fail to reach proper sanitizing temperatures after multiple cycles. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was replaced and the machine was observed to be reaching temperatures over 160F. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are frequently checked with test kits (in this case a maximum register thermometer or test strip) to verify proper sanitizing temperatures (160-194F).
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple foods in cold holding to be held past their seven day date marking period:
1) Cut grape tomatoes dated 4/21 in a prep cooler.
2) Cooked ribs dated 4/21 in the walk in cooler.
CORRECTED- Foods were removed from service to be discarded. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked if held over 24 hours to be used or discarded within seven days. The day of preparation counts as day 1 (foods dated 4/21 were to be used or discarded by 4/27- “plus 6”).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
findings.comment: No consumer advisory was available in the menus or posted otherwise in the facility. The inspector can bring consumer advisory signs to display during the 5/8 follow up until a new menu is printed. The increased risk of food-borne illness by consuming raw or undercooked animal proteins must be available and communicated to consumers.
findings.citation_text: 3-603.11(A) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (A) Except as specified in 3-401.11(C) and Subparagraph 3-401.11(D)(4) and under 3-801.11(C), if an animal FOOD such as beef, EGGS, FISH, lamb, milk, pork, POULTRY, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in READY-TO-EAT form or as an ingredient in another READY-TO-EAT FOOD, the PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of the significantly increased RISK of consuming such FOODS by way of a DISCLOSURE and REMINDER, as specified in (B) and (C) of this section using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility to not have a maximum heat registering test strip or dish plate to verify heat sanitizing temperatures for the dish machine. Devices used for sanitation of food contact surfaces must have a test kits to verify proper heat sanitizing temperatures. Inspector will return on or by 5/8 to ensure a maximum heat registering dish puck or test strips have been purchased and are in use.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the ice machine baffle to contain a small amount of soils. Discussed with PIC, and PIC had it cleaned and sanitized right away. Baffles can accumulate soil very fast; Ensure the baffle is cleaned regularly enough to keep it clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 5 flies in the downstairs bar. The flies were concentrated on the floor behind the ice machine. Facility already has a fruit fly trap set up to catch flies. Increased pest control measures may result in more success in dealing with the flies. Ensure flies are eradicated to protect food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1. Inspector observed the dish storage shelves in the facility to be dusty and tarnished. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that the shelves are going to be cleaned soon and liners will be applied to each shelf. Ensure the shelves are maintained in a way that keeps them free of dust and debris.

2. Inspector observed the tops of the cook line equipment to contain dust and food debris. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that the equipment is cleaned by the hood company regularly. Inspector recommends performing ancillary cleanings to keep surfaces free of debris between steam cleanings.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple hand sinks to not have paper towels. Reminded PIC of proper use of paper towels at hand sinks. PIC replaced paper towels at all sinks without paper towels. Ensure hand sinks are properly socked with paper towels at all times. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed two cold-holding units not holding temperature. 

The first unit was a double door cooler on the cook line. The food in the cooler was observed to be 50 F throughout (probed cottage cheese and grits). Ambient air was measured between 50-60F. Educated PIC on the state of the cold holding unit. PIC stated that cooler was in defrost mode. PIC threw away all food in cooler. Ensure food is kept at 41F or below during cold holding.

The second unit was the far prep table. Most foods in prep table (sauces, cheeses, and cut cherry tomatoes) were probed at 50-55 F. Educated PIC on high temps in the prep table. PIC voluntarily threw out all items in the prep table, even those that were not TCS. Prep cooler under prep table was holding temperature fine. Ensure prep table is kept at or below 41F.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a prep table to not be holding temperature. Most foods in prep table were probed between 50-55F. Educated PIC on proper cold holding. Ensure the prep table is serviced to facilitate adequate cold holding. Inspector will return 12/27/2024 to re-asses cooler.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon arrival, the hand washing sink by the office in the kitchen was out of hand soap.  Discussed with PIC, COS.  Ensure hand soap is available at all hand sinks at all times.

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer buckets in kitchen had a concentration of 100 ppm (q).  The sanitizer dispenser in the kitchen above the 3 part sink is not working properly, the sanitizer was not fully dispensing out of the line.  Discussed with PIC, do not use this sanitizer dispenser until it working properly.  Ensure EcoLab is contacted to repair the dispenser, in the meantime, use the dispenser in the dish room or use the tablets.  A follow-up will occur on 7/30/24 to check on sanitizer dispenser.

(B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Multiple items in the warmers had temperatures of 112-120F (probed) and an ambient temperature of 112F.  PIC stated they had just been put in there after the lunch period.  The gravies were warmed back up to 165, the other items were put in the other warmer.  After the items had been removed, the warmer was back up to an ambient temperature of 140F.  Ensure foods are promptly moved to the warmer from hot holding to prevent contamination.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Two containers of cheese sauce held on the steam table were observed to have a temperature (probed) of 130F.  Discussed with PIC, sauces were put back on the stove and warmed back up to 165F and also turned the temperature up on the steam table.  Ensure temperature of all items on the steam table are checked regularly to prevent contamination.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The prep cooler on the main line in the kitchen by the toasters was observed to have an ambient temperature of approximately 46-47F.  After using a probe thermometer to check the temperature of various food items, the temperatures ranged from 45-50F.  All items that had just been put in the cooler on this day were moved to a different cooler to cool to 41F.  Other items that had been kept in the prep cooler since 7/17/24 or an earlier date were discarded.  Do not use this prep cooler until it is repaired and properly holding the correct temperature of 41F or lower.  A follow-up will be conducted on 7/30/24.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Multiple items in different coolers were observed to be held past the 7 day maximum or not labeled.   There was also a block of cheese and shredded cheese containing mold.  A container of half and half in the downstairs bar was also observed to be not date marked. Discussed with PIC, all items were discarded.  Ensure the dates on all items are checked regularly and discarded if past the 7 day maximum.  

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Multiple drain flies were observed in the downstairs bar.  Facilities shall be free of pests to prevent an infestation and contamination of food.   Ensure methods of pest control are carried out to eliminate or control pests.  Ensure drains are inspected routinely to control and monitor pests.  

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

(C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.
